A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VGFM research, with matching authors, central formulation and retained experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison; v2 additionally contains a conference checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original VGFM experiments on synthetic and real single-cell datasets, including quantitative comparisons, loss ablations and mouse hematopoiesis results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds Pancreas evaluations, growth-rate correlations, predictive uncertainty estimates, sampling-bias tests and Sinkhorn-loss experiments.

M1.justification: v2 adds VGFM(*), which replaces the original Wasserstein distribution-fitting loss with Sinkhorn divergence (Table 3; Appendix B.6). Appendix B.2 also introduces dropout-based uncertainty inference. These are limited adaptations; the original semi-relaxed transport construction, joint matching formulation and training algorithm remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds developing mouse Pancreas data at days 14.5 and 15.5, evaluated using 2,000 highly variable genes, extending real biological coverage beyond the retained embeddings. It also introduces a biased-observation scenario by perturbing simulated branch proportions. Simulation Gene, Dyngen, Gaussian, EB, CITE and mouse hematopoiesis coverage remains.

E2.justification: Table 2 removes WLF-UOT from the EB/CITE hold-out comparison while retaining the other named comparators. Tables 3 and A-10 introduce comparisons with Sinkhorn-loss variants. The mouse hematopoiesis comparator set is unchanged, matching v1 Table A-6 to v2 Table A-9.

E3.justification: Section 4 revises the warm-up learning rate from 10^-4 to 10^-3 and the general warm-up schedule from 200–800 iterations to 500 for synthetic and 5,000 for real datasets. Appendices change Simulation Gene epsilon from 0.001 to 0.003, EB/CITE tau from 30 to 5, Dyngen batch size from 32 to 60, and hematopoiesis fitting epochs from 50 to 100. New analyses introduce additional evaluation protocols. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices B.2, B.6 and B.8 add intermediate-time growth-rate validation, branch/time uncertainty analysis, sampling-bias robustness, Sinkhorn regularization sensitivity, and Pancreas mean–variance and gene-attribution analyses. The Pancreas experiment also tests the distribution-fitting loss. v1's CITE training/hold-out loss curves in Figure A-14 are replaced by a with/without-loss trajectory comparison; the EB convergence analysis remains.

E5.justification: v1 lacks predictive uncertainty estimation or explicit repeated-seed reporting. v2 introduces variance estimation using dropout at rate 0.1 with five stochastic forward passes and reports sampling-bias results averaged over three random seeds (Tables A-7–A-8). This substantially adds statistical estimation, although main benchmark tables still lack error bars or significance tests. It does not establish increased run counts for retained benchmarks.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises VGFM's CITE W1 values from 0.650/34.182 to 0.745/37.386 and DeepRUOT's from 0.648/35.539 to 0.845/38.681; OT-MFM now leads both CITE columns. These accompany changed training settings and are not controlled across-version performance differences. Table 1 replaces UDSB's Gaussian W1/RME of 25.304/0.965 with nonconvergence. Substantial additions include Pancreas W1/RME of 24.416/0.017, growth correlations of 0.980–0.996, uncertainty and bias results, and Sinkhorn-variant scores and timing.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 corrects Equation A-15 by restoring the density factor p_t(x) inside the Benamou–Brenier kinetic-energy integral. The central proposition, endpoint-equivalence theorem, their proofs and the growth-energy minimization argument remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: joint velocity–growth modeling derived from semi-relaxed optimal transport, accurate state/mass reconstruction, and improved scalability and training efficiency. The added experiments support these existing claims without materially redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds a Malthusian-growth rationale for time-independent growth, an accumulated-error explanation for distribution fitting, and spatial/temporal interpretations of predictive uncertainty. Appendix B.8 links learned growth and gene-gradient rankings to Acinar/Ductal proliferation, adding substantive biological interpretation. The existing limitations concerning simulation dependence and potentially misleading observed cell counts remain.

D1.justification: v2 changes the code-release promise into a stated release with a concrete repository link in the abstract and checklist. Appendix B.6 newly identifies POT/emd and GeomLoss and explains gradient handling; new analyses document dropout, resampling and gene-selection details. Most architecture, batching and preprocessing information was already present in v1.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds optimal-transport application context, and references expand to recent unbalanced-dynamics work, Malthusian growth, Sinkhorn divergences and the Pancreas dataset. The Deep Momentum Multi-Marginal Schrödinger Bridge citation is removed. The central positioning against velocity-only flow matching and existing unbalanced dynamics models remains.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. v2 expands explanations in Sections 3.4 and A.4, adds focused experimental subsections and Appendix B.8, and includes acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist. These are localized narrative and structural extensions rather than a broad rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with five new experimental tables and Pancreas Figures A-15–A-18. Figure 2 is redrawn and relabeled, several trajectory plots are revised, Table 3 gains a variant row, and Figure A-14 replaces CITE loss curves with trajectory comparisons. The existing hematopoiesis table is merely renumbered from A-6 to A-9.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for biological applicability and reliability: it adds real 2,000-gene evaluation and interpretation, directly quantifies growth accuracy at unseen times, and tests sensitivity to biased observations. These address important gaps in v1's scalability and growth-validation evidence. The code-access information and corrected transport formula also help. The gains outweigh reduced comparator coverage and localized reporting problems, including conflicting RME values between Tables 3 and A-10 and claims of Sinkhorn improvement that overlook mixed metric outcomes.
